Shape.Name: Predefined process
Shape.Text:
Correlated Noise and or bands of RF in an image are called zippers. A single non-echo related frequency that is present in the scan room or leaked into the receiver will show up as a single, often dashed or dotted,line in the image. Multiple frequencies could generate multiple zippers. If multiple zippers are evenly spaced the cause may be an FM source or something else with sideband or harmonic frequencies. These non-echo related frequencies are encoded during normal acquisition and reconstructed into the images along with the other echo frequencies from the object being scanned. Zippers can occur when the RF shielding to the scan room has somehow been compromised. Shielded rooms are specified to attenuate RF signals by 100dB prior to the installation Penetration Panel. After installation of the penetration Panel, the room should still attenuate outside interference to about 60 – 80 dB. Breakdown in the shielded room usually occurs in doors or hatchways since they are frequently opened and closed and eventually wear out.
If the scan room’s RF shield is OK, it is possible that the source of the zipper is an electronic device inside the scan room. These potential sources can be turned off to isolate the causes of the zipper.

Shape.Name: Decision.19
Shape.Text: Able to reproduce zipper on a phantom?

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text: Run one of the customers protocols that produces the artifact on multiple phantoms in the middle of the bore. If the zipper still occurs, obviously it's not flow related. Proceed to the screen room checks.

Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text: Using multiple phantoms is a good way to rule out artifacts being patient related. However, since phantoms don't always demonstrate artifacts as well as patients do, you may not see any zipper on phantoms even if they are present on patients. This may be occurring since a patient can extend past the RF shield of the body coil and act as an antenna, pulling outside noise in.

Shape.Name: Decision.19
Shape.Text: Able to reproduce zipper on a phantom?

Shape.Name: Create request.8
Shape.Text: If the zipper is only in clinical imaging (not reproducible on phantoms) try swapping the phase and frequency to see if the zipper remains aligned to the vessel. If it remains aligned with the vessels with and without swapping phase and frequency it probably is a flow artifact. Review these images with support.

Shape.Name: Procedure.20
Shape.Text: If the artifact is really a flow related phenomena and not an RF zipper it will line up with the vessel regardless of which direction you use for frequency encoding. If the source is RF noise, it is unlikely that frequency would be encoded directly through a vessel both before and after phase and frequency are swapped.
